actions.description: Isolate an endpoint from the network via EDR to stop lateral movement.
Block an IP address at the firewall/XDR to stop C2 or exfiltration traffic.
Block network traffic to or from a suspicious IP, domain, port, or protocol at the firewall/XDR.
Block resolution or network access to a suspicious or malicious domain through DNS, firewall, or secure web gateway controls.
Block access to a specific malicious URL through the secure web gateway or proxy.
Increase monitoring of network connections created by processes on the affected host.
Enable SSL/TLS inspection for the relevant traffic scope to detect encrypted C2 communication.
Collect and review PowerShell execution history and command-line telemetry on the affected host.
Collect relevant endpoint artifacts such as process lists, autoruns, event logs, network connections, and suspicious files for investigation.
Capture a memory image from the affected endpoint for forensic analysis.
Create enhanced logging and alerting for unusual inbound or outbound data flows from the affected host.
Terminate a malicious process on the affected host.
Quarantine a malicious file/artifact detected on the host.
Remove a confirmed malicious file from the affected host.
Disable a compromised user/service account in the IdP.
Revoke active authentication sessions and refresh tokens for a potentially compromised account.
Force a credential reset for a compromised account.
Disable a confirmed malicious persistence mechanism such as a scheduled task, service, startup item, or autorun entry.
Block execution of a known malicious file hash through EDR or application control.
Start an on-demand EDR/antimalware scan on the affected endpoint.
Temporarily increase endpoint telemetry and process, authentication, and network event collection for the affected host.
Escalate the incident to a human SOC analyst without taking automated action.
No remediation required, close as benign/false positive.
